app_description: Minimal Node.js HTTP settings API built for auto-QA functional validation. Exposes a health check and a small in-memory settings store (theme, notifications) accessible via GET/POST /api/settings. Single-file app with no dependencies, deployed on Vercel.

deployment.model: Vercel preview deployment per PR (vercel.json routes all paths to index.js via @vercel/node)
deployment.ci_tool: Vercel (no GitHub Actions / other CI configured in repo)

auth.mechanism: none — API is fully unauthenticated; CORS open to *

database.type: none — in-memory JS object in index.js; state does not persist across serverless invocations

beliefs: Single-file Node.js app: all logic lives in index.js using the built-in http module.
Three endpoints: GET /health -> {status:'ok'}; GET /api/settings -> current settings; POST /api/settings -> merges JSON body into settings and returns updated object.
Default settings are { theme: 'light', notifications: true }. POST does a shallow merge with no validation of field names or types.
Invalid JSON on POST returns 400 {error:'invalid json'}. Unknown routes return 404 {error:'not found'}.
CORS is wide open (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *), OPTIONS preflight returns 200.
package.json has only a 'start' script (node index.js) and zero dependencies; no test framework, no linter, no build step.
Deployment is via Vercel; vercel.json routes every path to index.js compiled with @vercel/node. PR validation should hit the Vercel preview URL.
State is in-memory and per-instance — on Vercel serverless, POST changes are NOT guaranteed to persist between requests. PR tests should verify response shape rather than long-lived persistence.
Repo is brand new with a single commit ('init: settings API app'); no prior PR history to learn typical change patterns from.
No authentication, no database, no migrations, no seed scripts — validation can be done with simple HTTP requests.
gaps: No existing tests, test command, or coverage config — automated validation must be written from scratch against the live preview URL.
No OpenAPI / JSON schema — endpoint contracts are inferred from README and source only.
No CI workflows (no .github/, no GitHub Actions); unclear if Vercel previews are auto-created on PR or require manual setup / linked project.
Exact Vercel project name / preview URL pattern is unknown — must be discovered from PR comments or Vercel API at validation time.
Serverless persistence behavior is ambiguous: in-memory state may or may not survive between rapid requests depending on instance reuse; tests asserting persistence will be flaky.
No environment variables documented beyond PORT; unclear if any are configured in Vercel.
No input validation rules — unclear which fields/values should be considered 'valid' for POST /api/settings beyond JSON parseability.
Only one commit in git history, so PR-style change patterns (refactors, bugfixes, feature adds) cannot be inferred.
